findings.issue: No test files, test script, or test dependency anywhere in app/; all quality gates are the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add at least unit tests for the pure helpers in lib/api.js and route-handler tests (Gracile handlers are plain async functions, easy to invoke with fixture data) before the next refactor of the data layer.

findings.issue: catch-all turns every failure (API 500, transient network error, a nested getMove/getTypeInfo failure inside loadMoveRows) into a 404 'Not found' page; same pattern in routes/moves/[name].js:45-49, routes/abilities/[name].js:43-47 and routes/types/[name].js:69-73.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish ApiError status 404 from other errors (return 500 for those) and add tests for both paths — this masking bug is invisible to any happy-path check.

findings.issue: Combined filtering, page clamping (Math.min with totalPages), and the 48-per-page slice are untested; a refactor could double-apply a filter, break the clamp, or miscount without any failing signal.
findings.suggestion: Extract the filter/paginate step into a pure function and test it against the fixture data: no filters, each filter alone, filters combined, page out of range, zero matches.

findings.issue: Method-table construction (METHOD_ORDER first then alphabetical, empty methods dropped, ?game= query respected) and level-then-name sorting (sortMoveRows, :60-68) are untested.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test loadMoveRows + sortMoveRows with a small synthetic pokemon.moves payload covering two version groups, an out-of-order method set, and a missing-level entry.

findings.issue: Alternate-form exclusion (id < MAX_REGULAR_ID) and the species index sort are the linchpin of every list page; an off-by-one or a broken idFromUrl regex (:58-61, feeding Number.isFinite guards) would silently include forms >10000 or drop/duplicate species.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test idFromUrl, getSpeciesIndex and uniqueSpeciesFromPokemonReferences with URLs for regular, mega (id 10001) and female-form Pokémon.

findings.issue: Display-name rule helpers (humanize vs englishName, latest English flavor text with whitespace collapse, displayValue em-dash) encode most of the spec's naming rules and are untested.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven tests for humanize('mr-mime'), englishName fallback, latestEnglishFlavorText picking the last en entry and collapsing \n/\f, and displayValue(null).

findings.issue: Client filter flow (debounce, replaceState vs pushState, stale-response guard via requestNumber, popstate sync) has no coverage; a race-condition or URL-regression here is only caught by manual browser testing.
findings.suggestion: Add a small Playwright component/route test typing into search, asserting results update without Enter and the URL gains/loses params correctly.

findings.issue: Column sorting (ascending-first toggle, aria-sort updates, missing-values-last in both directions) is pure client logic with no tests; a comparator regression would reorder tables silently.
findings.suggestion: Test compareRows directly (it's a top-level function in the client script) or via DOM: click Power ascending with a null-power row and assert it stays last.

findings.issue: Promise cache evicts failed requests (request.catch(() => cache.delete(url))); dropping that line in a refactor would pin a rejected promise in the cache for the process lifetime — every subsequent request for that resource 404s via the catch-all.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test getJson with a failing then succeeding fetch stub to assert the failure is not cached.

findings.issue: The API-failure fallback renders a 200-looking shell with empty selects and '0 Pokémon' with status 500; nothing verifies this degraded state is sane.
findings.suggestion: A handler test with a rejected API stub asserting status 500 and a coherent error page.

summary: The app ships no tests of its own — no test script, runner, or spec file — so every behaviour guarantee lives in the external acceptance suite. The riskiest code (filtering/pagination, move-table assembly, form exclusion/dedup, error paths, all client-side interactivity) is exactly the kind that breaks silently under refactor. The catch-all 404 handlers are the most dangerous gap: they mask server-side API failures as 'Not found', which no happy-path test would ever reveal.
